title: The Volcano Behind the Bicycle
arc: hook_payoff / myth-adjacent reversal (hook poses a question, last beat answers it)
note: Durations in timing.json are ESTIMATES from word count. No voice-over exists yet. Final VO = Gemini TTS, one wav per beat in audio/vo/beat_NN.wav; run timing.py to re-clock.

beats.text: A volcano erupts in one corner of the world. Two years later, in another, a man gives up on horses.
April, eighteen fifteen. Tambora, in Indonesia, blows apart. The most powerful eruption in recorded history.
Ash and sulphur wrap the whole Earth. Sunlight dims. The planet cools.
Eighteen sixteen becomes the year without a summer. Harvests fail across Europe.
In Germany, oats, the fuel of every horse, run short. Horses starve. Many are slaughtered.
A German inventor named Karl Drais looks at the empty stables and asks: what if you didn't need a horse?
In eighteen seventeen he builds a wooden machine. Two wheels. No pedals. You push the ground away with your feet.
He rides it out of Mannheim, faster than anyone can walk. No oats required.
Historians still argue about the famine's role. But the timing is hard to ignore.
That machine is the ancestor of every bicycle. A reply to a volcano, twelve thousand kilometres away.
